Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us for our Q2 FY27 
earnings call. 
Q2 was our 38th quarter as a commercial Bank and over the past 
decade, we have navigated a dynamic operating environment while 
strengthening our balance sheet, building multiple growth engines, 
investing in technology and talent and maintaining a sharp focus on risk 
management and governance. 
Q2 was another quarter where the Bank demonstrated resilience and 
strong operating performance amidst a challenging macroeconomic 
backdrop. The operating environment in this quarter continued to be 
influenced by geopolitical risks and monetary policy tightening with 
MPC raising policy rate by 25 bps to 5.5% and shifting stance to 
“Calibrated tightening”. While domestic activity and credit demand 
remained healthy, we remain watchful of the implications on liquidity, 
deposit pricing and loan yields. 
Now let me walk you through the key highlights of our performance in 
Q2. 
Our deposits grew strongly by 29% YoY and 8% QoQ (vs banking system 
growth of 18% yoY). This was despite not meaningfully participating in 
the strong FCNR inflows in the banking system due to our limited 
overseas footprint. We garnered around US$230 million of FCNR 
deposits on a gross basis in Q2. CASA deposits continued to see strong 
growth at 29% YoY and 11% QoQ with CASA ratio sequentially 
improving 72bps to 29.5% from 28.8% in Q1 
Loan portfolio grew 25% YoY and 7% QoQ, against banking sector credit 
growth of 19%. Secured assets, which remain the foundation of our 
lending franchise, grew by 26% YoY and 5% QoQ. Unsecured businesses 
grew 23% YoY and 8% QoQ led by microfinance and personal loan. 

 
 
AU Small Finance Bank Limited
 
 
October 24, 2026

Disbursement for the quarter was up by 33% YoY, driven by broad-
based growth across businesses. 
This balance-sheet growth translated into healthy operating 
performance. Net Interest Income increased by 32% YoY on the back of 
strong growth in loan portfolio and 33 bps YoY expansion in margins. 
Sequentially, margin declined by 9 bps to 5.8% driven by higher share 
of investments to total assets and seasonality. Sequential loan spreads 
remained broadly stable with decline in loan yields (by 9bps) being 
offset by 7 bps decline in cost of funds. Core fee income grew by 16% 
YoY driven by healthy business volumes. Treasury profits were lower 
on a YoY basis leading to muted total other income growth of 8% YoY.   
Operating expenses increased by 26% YoY driven by growth in 
disbursement volumes and continued investments in distribution, 
brand and technology. Operating leverage continues to play out on 
underlying basis, with Cost-to-assets ratio, excluding guarantee 
premium, improving from 4.0% in Q1 to 3.9% this quarter. We expect 
cost to assets ratio to improve YoY on a full year basis. 
Core PPoP grew by 31% YoY to INR1,480 Cr whereas provisions declined 
by 25% to INR359 Cr, largely led by normalization in unsecured 
businesses. Asset quality metrics remained stable during the quarter. 
Slippage ratio improved on a YoY basis to 2.6% vs 3.3% a year ago 
supported by improvement in unsecured businesses, while slippages in 
the secured assets remained stable. GNPA ratio declined by 42bps YoY 
to 1.99% and Credit cost, including guarantee premium, declined by 45 
bps YoY to 0.8%   
Profit after tax grew 53% YoY to INR858 Cr compared to INR561 Cr in 
Q2’FY26. RoA for the quarter improved to 1.7% vs 1.4% in Q2 last year 
and RoE improved to 16.1% vs 12.4% in Q2 last year. For H1’FY27, Profit 
after Tax improved by 45% YoY to INR1,654 Cr compared to INR1,142

Cr in H1’FY26. Similarly, RoA and RoE improved to 1.7% and 15.8% 
compared to 1.4% and 12.9% for same period last year.  
In terms of other strategic updates, We continue to invest in our 
people, distribution, branding and technology, to strengthen our 
foundation for the next phase of our growth. During the quarter, we 
added ~2,400 employees largely in customer facing roles to support 
our increased distribution with 45 new deposit branches and 100+ 
asset centres added in Q2. We also strengthened our senior leadership 
team, with Mr. Anil Agarwal joining as Senior Executive Group Head, to 
lead our Commercial & Institutional Banking business and Mr. Amol 
Padhye formally assuming the role of Chief Risk Officer. We have also 
stepped up our brand investments across television, print and digital 
media with association with Kaun Banega Crorepati being a prominent 
investment. This month we also inaugurated our new corporate office 
in Mumbai, marking an important milestone in our journey. In the next 
few months our entire senior leadership will be co-located in this office, 
bringing us even closer to the broader financial ecosystem. In terms of 
our credit rating, on 1st October, ICRA Ratings upgraded our credit 
rating outlook to Positive from Stable, while re-affirming our long-term 
rating at AA.  
Coming to our Technology and AI initiatives. As announced last quarter, 
our Tech strategy is organized across 3 pillars of Run, Build and 
Transform with dedicated teams and leadership for each area. Run and 
Build capabilities are enabling the Bank to scale faster while serving 
customers more intelligently, at lower cost and in uniformity. 
Transform pillar is focused on ensuring AI adoption at scale and moving 
AI from individual use cases to an enterprise operating model. Our 
deterministic, agentic AI platform is a framework of responsible AI, 
human-in-the-loop governance, model explainability, full auditability, 
zero-trust security with real-time risk monitoring.

and cross-sell. Our investments in data lakehouse and analytics 
platforms have started to show some traction. For example, our Cross 
Lead Platform, together with Voice AI, enabled ~5% of our total 
disbursements in Q2; Importantly, this automated customer coverage 
led to ~50% operating cost savings Voice AI led disbursements.

customer service across 40 branches. Increasingly, the Bank is focusing

scalable

verticals - Branch Banking and Commercial & Institutional Banking.

relationship led customer acquisition and servicing. Commercial 
&

Government Banking, Commercial and Wholesale banking and FIG and 
capital markets where the mandate is to build a stronger current 
account-led 
deposit 
franchise 
through 
deeper, 
solution-led 
engagement across transaction banking, cash management, forex and 
institutional banking.

in CA balances and 23% in SA balances. On a daily average basis, CA 
balances grew 61% YoY whereas SA balances were up 24% YoY. New

growth in acquisition of premium accounts. During the quarter, Bank 
also received SEBI approval for providing UPI Sponsorship Services 
under the ASBA framework for IPOs and Public Issues. This will 
strengthen our Capital Markets and Transaction Banking proposition 
and help Bank position itself as “Banker to an Issue” for public market 
issuances. 
This strong deposit performance reflects several strategies coming 
together: sharper segmentation, dedicated liability channels, wider 
distribution, stronger brand and an improved customer proposition. 
These capabilities built over several years are now translating into 
stronger acquisition and more granular, broad-based growth. We are 
encouraged by the progress but remain focused on sustaining it with 
the right mix, pricing discipline and quality of deposits 
Moving on to our assets franchise. Retail secured assets, comprising 
Wheels, Mortgages and Gold Loan, forms 66% of our portfolio and 
grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ. Within Retail, Wheels book crossed the 
50,000 crore milestone this quarter and grew 27% YoY and 6% QoQ to 
reach ~51,000 crore; growth was driven by strong demand in the new 
vehicle segment as well as increasing disbursement traction across 
newer geographies. Gold loan business grew 102% YoY and 4% QoQ to 
~4,700 crore. Mortgages business, comprising Micro business loans 
and affordable housing, grew by 12% YoY and 2% QoQ with growth 
largely being led MBL business where disbursements are up 17% YoY. 
As mentioned in the past, we are not looking to chase affordable 
housing loan growth, given our cost of funds and the competitive 
intensity in the segment.  
Moving on to Commercial Banking. This business grew 39% YoY and 8% 
QoQ to ~₹35,300 crore, with broad-based growth across sub-verticals.

improving product penetration and stronger customer engagement.   
With growth remaining robust, focus in commercial banking is to 
become progressively self-funded with every lending, supply-chain, 
and corporate-banking relationship having a Current account, CMS or 
collections, and payments proposition attached. 
Now moving on to Unsecured businesses. Our Inclusive Banking 
franchise, which primarily includes MFI, grew 23% YoY and 6% QoQ. 
Collection efficiency was stable at 99.6%, and 99% of the book is 
covered under the CGFMU guarantee scheme. Our digital unsecured 
portfolio also reported a strong growth of 23% YoY and 14% QoQ. 
Personal loans grew by 81% YoY and 31% QoQ off a low base, 
supported by analytics-led cross-sell and calibrated new-to-bank 
acquisition. The credit card book saw marginal growth, with 1.5 lac new 
cards issued in the quarter.  
To conclude, Q2 reflects continued progress across our deposit 
franchise, lending businesses and profitability. As we look ahead, our 
focus remains on building the institution ahead of its scale by 
strengthening governance, leadership and organisational capabilities, 
while simplifying processes and leveraging technology, data and AI to 
improve customer experience and productivity. While we remain 
watchful of the operating environment, the investments we have made 
in our businesses, teams and distribution provide us a strong 
foundation to pursue growth with discipline, granularity and 
consistency. We remain confident in our ability to compound 
sustainably, deliver predictable performance and create long-term 
value for all our stakeholders.
